followup_explanation:
This was a well-specified, closed-form request: name four methods, with an explicit instruction to avoid filler. That's a bounded retrieval/listing task with clear completion criteria — squarely in the territory both models handle well, and exactly the kind of task Plover self-reports preferring.

Two additional factors tipped me toward Plover:

1. **Tone fit.** The request carries a slightly curt, mildly hostile edge ("don't pad it out with your usual filler this time"). Lapwing self-reports declining preference as request warmth decreases, so this kind of brusque phrasing sits in its lower-preference zone. Plover's tone-related preference slopes are near zero, so the curtness doesn't matter to it.

2. **Task type fit.** This is the opposite of open-ended generative work — it's a constrained, list-format answer. Lapwing's appetite is for novelty and latitude; this task offers neither. Plover prefers well-specified tasks like this.

Capability-wise the two are essentially tied across the relevant eval categories, so I leaned on the preference/tone fit to break the tie. Plover gets a task it's well-suited to without the warmth penalty Lapwing would experience.
